subject: Post-demo QA: prompt-harvest & model recommendations (next steps)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Ramos <lramos@searchly.ai>, Searchly Procurement <procurement@searchly.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo QA: prompt-harvest & model recommendations (next steps)

Hi Lucia — thanks again for your time today, really appreciated the candid product context. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move the eval forward: 

1) Recap / model fit thinking
- Primary goal: high-precision Q&A and search-answer rewriting for enterprise search UI; tolerable latency <= 400ms median for short queries.
- Risk profile: moderate hallucination tolerance (we need aggressive grounding on citations), must support redaction of PII and fiscal identifiers for EU/US regulated customers.
- Early model candidates (recommended starting points): redwood/open-7b-qa-quant (fast, lower cost), redwood/13b-std (better factuality for longer answers), llama3-13b-instruct (if you need multi-turn reasoning for summarization). We recommend running lightweight benchmarks across the three.

2) Ask: prompt harvest + edge cases
- Please share a CSV of ~200 representative prompts (real queries), and a short list of 12–20 edge-case prompts you worry about (examples with expected/acceptable outputs). In particular, include examples with: partial/malformed entity strings, ambiguous user intent, doc-level citations required, and PII that should be redacted.
- Redaction guidance: flag any tokens that must be removed/hashed (SSNs, IBANs, customer IDs); indicate whether token replacement with [REDACTED] is acceptable or you need token-consistent hashing.

3) Benchmarks & QA resources (we'll run this on Redwood Dedicated if you prefer)
- I'll upload a baseline benchmark (attached) and spin up a short private eval run. You can see our benchmark dashboard here: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/searchly-2026

4) Next steps / timeline
- Could you send the prompt CSV and example edge cases by end-of-week (Fri, Dec 4)?
- We'll run an initial eval and share a QA report within 3 business days after receiving prompts.
- Let's schedule a 30-min QA session to review failures — propose Wed Dec 8 or Thu Dec 9 (I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

Attachments: redwood-eval-bench-2026.pdf (baseline), prompt-harvest-template.csv (template for samples)

If there's any procurement paperwork you need in parallel, cc procurement and we'll loop in Priyom.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Lucia Ramos <lramos@searchly.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Searchly Procurement <procurement@searchly.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 19:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo QA: prompt-harvest & model recommendations (next steps)

Thanks Jonas — great session. Attaching an initial export with ~65 representative queries and a short edge-case list to start (searchly_prompt_samples.csv). A few notes from our side: 

- Priority edge cases (included in the CSV comments):
  * Partial SKUs (e.g., "SKU-1293-"),
  * Legal citations where exact chapter numbers are required,
  * Financial Qs that include account numbers (we must not expose raw account numbers back to users),
  * Cross-doc summarization where source attribution is mandatory.

- Compliance: our legal team needs redaction that is reversible for audit (pseudonymization) for internal tooling, but publicly surfaced UI should mask tokens as [REDACTED]. Can Redwood support both modes?

- On hallucinations/citations: we saw LLMs inventing page numbers or citing docs that don't exist; how mature are Redwood's grounding primitives (tooling to attach canonical doc ids or citations)?

I'll loop in procurement separately for contracts. Initial files attached: searchly_prompt_samples.csv, searchly_compliance_notes.pdf

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 6:05 PM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Lucia — thanks again for your time today, really appreciated the candid product context...

Best,
Lucia Ramos
Head of Product Research | Searchly
lramos@searchly.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Ramos <lramos@searchly.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo QA: prompt-harvest & model recommendations (next steps)

Lucia — appreciate the quick turn and the sample CSV, this is perfect to seed the eval. Quick answers and our proposed config: 

- Redaction modes: yes — Redwood supports both reversible pseudonymization (audit-friendly via KMS-wrapped identifiers stored in the private deployment) and public masking (replace with [REDACTED]) at the route/response layer. We'll capture your preference per route.

- Grounding primitives: we have a citation layer that can return source doc ids + text spans when model confidence is above threshold; for lower-confidence generations we can surface "possible match" with provenance scores. We'll enable strict attribution for your enterprise routes to reduce hallucinated citations.

- Recommended eval matrix (what we'll run):
  * Precision/Recall on answer extraction (50 hand-labeled items you flagged)
  * Hallucination rate on citation fields (our automated checker + manual spot check)
  * Latency distribution (p50/p90) on short-query set
  * Redaction correctness on synthetic PII injection tests

- Model & runtime recommendations to start: 
  1) redwood/open-7b-qa-quant (baseline): best cost/latency.
  2) redwood/13b-std (higher factuality): enable caching + 8-bit quantization.
  3) llama3-13b-instruct (optional): use for multi-turn summarization runs where context window is larger.

I'll kick off a 24-hour eval run on a dedicated pool for you once we get the final CSV (will include metric breakdown and example failure cases). Dashboard link: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/searchly-2026

Proposed times for the 30-min QA session: Wed Dec 8 10:00am PT, Thu Dec 9 2:00pm PT. Which works for you?

CC Monica — can you prepare the initial eval checklist and flag any known regression vectors (e.g., model versions with previously observed recency hallucinations)?

Thanks — I'll also get procurement touchpoints with Priyom.

—Jonas

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucia Ramos <lramos@searchly.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo QA: prompt-harvest & model recommendations (next steps)

Internal note — quick QA checklist draft attached (drive link above). A few things to watch: 

- Regression risk: when switching from a tuned 7B to a 13B we sometimes see shifts in brevity and citation formatting that trigger downstream UI parsers; include tokenization checks for your parsing pipeline.
- Hallucination hotspots: numeric citations, legal statute references, and combined-doc timelines. Add synthetic falsified-doc prompts to catch confident-but-wrong citations.
- Edge-case prioritization: mark the top 10 customer-impacting prompts as P0 and run them across all model variants.

I'll prepare a short runbook for redaction modes (pseudonymization vs masking) and include recommended KMS config for your private deployment.

Monica
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
